description: Household Evacuation Responses to the Los Angeles Wildfire Emergency is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Evelyn Blumenberg, University of California Los Angeles (ucla.edu). There is a significant gap in research on human behavior in fire research. Existing research on fire evacuation largely centers on whether, when, and how to evacuate; these studies allow agencies to better predict evacuation travel behavior and to implement effective traffic management measures. Some of these studies incorporate behavioral variability in travel demand. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (CSV, XLSX). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-5493-2446. Keywords: household evacuation, Los Angeles wildfires, wildfire emergency, built environment, evacuation experience, random sample survey. Published 2026-08-05. Facility named: SSEER - Social Science Extreme Events Research. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
